idiom_name: small struct implementing a local Publisher/Subscriber interface over amqp091-go Channel.Publish/Consume
implementation_notes: Go collapses the adapter into an interface plus a thin struct: declare the application-facing port (`type OrderPublisher interface { Publish(ctx context.Context, o Order) error }`) and implement it with amqp091-go's Channel.PublishWithContext, keeping amqp types out of the interface. The inbound direction consumes the `<-chan amqp.Delivery` returned by Channel.Consume and invokes the application function per delivery with an explicit Ack/Nack, so goroutines and channels replace the listener/factory structure. If you prefer a library over a dozen lines of glue, watermill provides Publisher/Subscriber interfaces with RabbitMQ/Kafka/PostgreSQL implementations, but the plain interface over the client is the idiomatic Go form.
pitfalls: The Delivery channel is closed by the library when the connection drops: a range loop over it ends silently, so the adapter must detect the close reason and resubscribe instead of treating it as shutdown.
Acking every delivery regardless of handler outcome turns at-least-once into at-most-once; use Nack(requeue) and keep handlers idempotent.
A channel closed by a protocol error stays unusable: the adapter must reopen the channel (or connection) after a failure rather than reusing it.
